title: French Onion Soup
subtitle: deeply caramelized onions in a rich beef broth under toasted baguette and bubbling, browned Gruyère
imageAlt: A crock of French onion soup topped with a toasted baguette slice and browned, bubbling melted cheese on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 6 bowls: dinner for two, plus 4 for lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The onions take about an hour to caramelize; low and slow is the whole secret.
You need oven-safe bowls for the classic cheese top, or broil the cheese toasts on a sheet and float them.

items.name: yellow onions
items.note: about 6 large, halved and thinly sliced

steps.title: Caramelize
steps.text: Melt the butter with the oil in a large heavy pot over medium. Add the onions, sugar and salt, cover and cook 10 minutes until they collapse. Uncover, lower to medium-low and cook 50–60 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the bottom, until deep golden brown. Add a splash of water if they catch.

steps.title: Broth
steps.text: Stir in the flour for 1 minute. Slowly add the broth, scraping up all the brown bits, then the Worcestershire, dried thyme, bay leaf and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Meanwhile, heat the broiler. Toast the baguette slices on a baking sheet 1–2 minutes a side until dry and golden.

steps.title: Broil
steps.text: Discard the bay leaf. Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls on a baking sheet, float a toast or two on each and cover with the Gruyère. Broil 2–4 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots. Warn everyone: the bowls are very hot.

fixIt.fix: Lower the heat and add 2 tbsp water, scraping the brown bits back in.
The onions needed longer; simmer 10 minutes more with another 1 tsp Worcestershire.
Toast the bread until fully dry before it goes on the soup.

saleTip: A 3 lb bag of onions is often $1.99 at No Frills; Gruyère is cheaper in the deli cheese case than pre-shredded.
swap: Swiss or mozzarella for Gruyère. Slow cooker: caramelize the onions on high 8–10 hours with the lid ajar, stirring a few times.
leftovers: Freeze the soup without the bread and cheese; make fresh toasts when you reheat.
doneness: No raw meat to cook (beef broth base). Reheat the soup to a simmer, 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, leftovers).
source: Based on tested French onion soup methods (Ricardo, America's Test Kitchen): onions caramelized low and slow about an hour, simmered in beef broth with thyme and bay, topped with toasted baguette and broiled Gruyère.
prepAhead: Make the soup up to 3 days ahead or freeze it up to 3 months; it tastes even better.
Toast the baguette slices up to 2 days ahead and keep them in a bag.
reheat: Covered over medium until simmering, 74°C (165°F), then top and broil.

basic.note: Caramelized onion soup with cheese toast; no Worcestershire, dried thyme or bay.

stepNotes.1: Basic: just the broth and pepper.

fancy.note: A splash of red wine in the onions and extra Parmesan in the cheese top.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: before the flour, pour in the wine and boil 3 minutes, scraping, until almost gone.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: mix the Parmesan into the Gruyère.

plating: Bowls on small plates with a folded napkin under them.
A spoon and a steak knife for the cheese.

why.0-2: Slow cooking turns the onions' sugars deep brown and sweet; that's the soup's flavour.
why.1-1: Gruyère melts smoothly and browns with a nutty, salty flavour.
why.0-5: A little flour gives the broth body.

funFact: French onion soup was the classic late-night meal at Les Halles, Paris's old central market, served to market workers and night owls.
drink: A dry white like Pinot Grigio, or apple cider.
